L217: “The tool I wish I’d been given as a child”
L218: I started the drums at 4, and music theory put me off playing, so I learned by ear. At 12, at the piano, I realised my memory wasn’t built to decode abstract notes: it’s visual-motor and spatial. With the handpan I hit the same wall: spaceships with no pilot’s manual. So I drew. From those drawings came the tool I wish I’d been given: music theory made visible, in languages a child can understand.
